take: Iranian crude disappearing from the market just as China’s independent refiners return for more is the key bullish crude story, tightening the medium-sour barrel pool that Asian teapots rely on and lending support to Brent and Dubai spreads. The Strait of Hormuz remains the second theme, with an LNG tanker and two other tankers reportedly struck by unknown projectiles even as conflicting data points to a 98% recovery in Gulf transit, so freight war-risk premia and LNG routing costs stay bid. The positioning angle sits in the diesel complex, where Oilprice argues the shortfall has existed since at least 2020 and is not simply an Iran-war artefact, meaning elevated crack spreads are structural rather than a spike to fade. The cross-market link is bunker versus gasoil: with alternative-fuel newbuilds outpacing trained crews and Hormuz risk lifting LNG carrier insurance, HSFO and VLSFO economics will diverge from distillate cracks as scrubber-fitted tonnage gets rerated. Watch the next 24 hours for any UKMTO or UKMTO-style confirmation on Hormuz transits and for signs China’s teapot buying translates into physical Dubai cargoes, whilst keeping an eye on the Dallas Fed survey showing crude swinging from $67 to $107 in under three months.

items.title: Public companies produce most U.S. crude oil and natural gas
items.summary: Publicly traded companies represent a tiny share of the total number of companies producing crude oil and natural gas in the United States, but they make up a large share of U.S. production. In 2025, publicly traded companies accounted for just 2% of about 12,000 oil and natural gas producers but produced 68% of the crude oil and natural gas in the Lower 48 states.

items.title: What goes into diesel prices?
items.summary: The price of distillate fuel oil, often sold as diesel, is driven by the price of crude oil, retail margins, distribution costs, taxes, and crack spreads, the indicator we use for refining margins. Tight global supplies of distillate fuel oil and elevated crude oil prices have driven prices higher in recent months.
